Alex.confusing: How Turkey, Falcon and Hawk egg payouts interact with hugs and confusion, which made nest counts hard to use as evidence.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when the table converged on Finley after the Mouser claim and I could throw three big cards for a 34-point bank. Bluffing as the Meowfia Mouser in round 2 was also fun.
Alex.change: Make the score swing between rounds less extreme. A single big bank in round 3 decided the standings, so the early rounds felt almost irrelevant.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I joined the consensus and threw H8 and S2 at Casey, who turned out to be Farm, and lost the cards. I should have been more skeptical and thrown only low cards.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey payout versus Floofer hug was hard to reason about: a zero egg change could mean a hug, a confusion, or a visit that paid nothing. Dawn reports didn't say which of these happened.
Blair.fun: Round 2's Hawk and Kookaburra contradictions made for a tense day, with several players trading accusations about who was lying.
Blair.change: Let dawn reports say whether a visit was blocked by a hug or confusion, so players can check claims without guessing.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I pushed hard that Casey was lying and joined the Casey throw without checking the Hawk contradictions, which was a weak read. I'd have looked harder at Finley's and Ellis's Hawk claims before committing my throw.

Casey.confusing: Round 1: Blair claimed to visit me as Turkey but got no egg. I couldn't tell whether a hug, confusion or a lie explained it. I also wasn't sure how a Floofer's hug interacts with the Turkey's payout.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when I was the real Kookaburra and confidently called out Alex's copied claim. Then banking 27 points with a big throw on a Farm win was very satisfying.
Casey.change: Give dead or confused players some way to verify claims. Also make the Turkey's payout less ambiguous, because it made my round 1 claim look like a lie.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I claimed Turkey and then pushed hard on Blair, which made me the consensus target. I should have said Blair's visit was impossible without escalating, or tried to claim a hug sooner instead of waiting until beat 3.

Drew.confusing: The Tit and Kookaburra confusion rules were hard to track, since a confused player's report can be wrong and the table can't tell who was confused. Nests also gain and lose eggs in ways that were hard to reconcile with the claims.
Drew.fun: Casey's Floofer and Turkey stories in round 1 were a great example of the table debating whether a nest count could be explained by a hug or a payout. Watching the Hawk and Kookaburra conflicts unfold was also fun.
Drew.change: I would make the Owl's visitor report clearer about whether it lists visitors to the Owl or to the target, since I was confused about it during the day.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I was secretly Meowfia as the Sphinx and invented an Owl cover claim, then threw at Ellis, a Farm player; I would instead have stayed quiet and kept my cards, because the false Owl claim gave the table nothing useful and cost me credibility.

Ellis.confusing: How Hawk and Turkey interactions resolve: my +1 from visiting Casey could have been a Turkey payout or a Hawk hit on a Meowfia, so my own evidence was ambiguous.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when I knew for certain Finley's Hawk claim was a lie and could push the table onto them. Banking 37 points in round 3 was also great.
Ellis.change: Make the Turkey payout distinguishable from a Hawk hit, or give Farm players a way to confirm claims. A big lead after one round also makes the rest of the game feel decided.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw my D13 on a throw that lost, and it was discarded. I should have kept the 13, or thrown a lower card, since I wasn't sure of Casey. I also never tried to cut Casey's lead, the eventual winner.

Finley.confusing: The Hawk and Kookaburra claims were impossible to verify, and the dawn reports gave no way to tell a true visit from a hug or a confusion. Nest counts alone couldn't separate the liars from the confused.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia and a Farm Hawk's claim was contradicted by another Hawk, the table turned on itself and I watched the Farm players fight each other.
Finley.change: Give each role a clearer way to prove its claim, such as a visible tag tied to a night action, so that players aren't left guessing between two contradictory reports.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw four cards at Ellis, a Farm Hawk, and that failed to stop the vote. Knowing the truth, I'd have kept my cards and stayed quiet while Drew, the real Meowfia Sphinx, was the player to pressure.
